images.title: Straight and parallel after all
images.purpose: Show that two lines that look bent among spokes are really parallel, by a measured equal gap.
images.composition: Two panels side by side with a thin grey divider: the illusion on the left, the check on the right.
exact_structure: Left panel: two vertical straight teal (#0072B2) lines, 4 units apart, drawn over a burst of 12 thin grey (#6B7280) spokes radiating from a centre between the lines, so the lines look bent outwards in the middle.
Right panel: the same two vertical teal lines, with the same spokes drawn very faint.
A long straight edge (ruler) in amber (#E69F00) lies against the left teal line in the right panel.
Three equal horizontal double headed arrows between the two lines, at the top, the middle and the bottom, in reddish purple (#CC79A7), each labelled same.
rejection: the three gap arrows of different lengths
more or fewer than three gap arrows
images.takeaway: A ruler and equal gaps show the lines are straight and parallel, whatever the eye seems to see.
images.description: Left, two lines look bent among spokes; right, a ruler and three equal gaps show they are straight and parallel.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students compare the left picture with the measured check on the right.

image_decisions.why: One illusion with its check is enough to show trust the test, not the eye.
